findings.title: AttributeError: calling cache_clear() on a function without lru_cache decorator
findings.description: The `reset_cache` function calls `get_supported_language_variant.cache_clear()`, but the refactored `get_supported_language_variant` is no longer decorated with `@functools.lru_cache`. A plain Python function does not have a `cache_clear` attribute, so this call will raise `AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'cache_clear'` every time `reset_cache` is invoked with `setting` in `("LANGUAGES", "LANGUAGE_CODE")`. This is triggered whenever Django's language settings are changed at runtime (e.g., via `override_settings` in tests, or dynamic configuration), causing a hard crash in the cache-reset path.
findings.suggestion: Since the `lru_cache` decorator has been removed from the language-variant lookup, the `cache_clear()` call is no longer needed. Remove the line `get_supported_language_variant.cache_clear()` from `reset_cache`. If you still want to clear any internal caching, ensure the function actually has a cache (re-add `@functools.lru_cache` with a bounded `maxsize`) or remove the call entirely.
